findings.title: A4-P2 is structurally dead under the frozen R2 rule: the family's index-only control is its own arm by construction, so R2 vetoes every A4-P2 arm exactly when R1 passes -- 3 of 6 trial cells (50% of budget) cannot produce a survivor regardless of outcomes
findings.description: The frozen A4-P2 arm state_source_law computes the decision state from VIX9D/VIX/VIX3M index closes ONLY (selection_freeze.json arm configs; arms.SlopeAccelerationRunner.build_state consumes ctx['index'] only). battery.index_only_shadow for FAMILY_A4_P2 sets state = runner.build_state(ctx) -- literally the arm's own state -- and records distinct_from_arm=None ('shadow == arm state by construction (disclosed)'), visible in z_cell_1. At E, the scored control book is therefore IDENTICAL to the arm book, so index_control_expectancy == arm_expectancy. evaluator.control_reproduces(c,a) returns True iff c>0 and a!=0 and c >= 0.5*a; evaluate_r2 returns FAIL (VETO) when True. Hence for every A4-P2 arm: R2 FAILS iff arm expectancy > 0, which is exactly R1's pass condition. No A4-P2 arm can reach PROVISIONAL_STAGE_A_SURVIVOR under the committed frozen evaluator; the only world where R2 does not fire is expectancy <= 0, where R1 kills the arm anyway. This is also the D1 A4-P2 bytes' own kill clause ('If the ETP-leg placement is not distinct from its own index re-clock ... the proposal dies as an index re-clock') firing tautologically -- the information needed to know this was fully available outcome-blind at S, yet the S freeze booked A4-P2 into budget cells 1-3 and declares its family falsification binding site as R1/R5 (cost ceiling), never disclosing that R2 is a guaranteed structural death. battery.py discloses the structural identity but not its R2 consequence. Either the freeze is internally contradictory (3 cells booked into a family already dead by its own preregistered kill clause), or the E phase must deviate from the frozen evaluator semantics (post-freeze rule change, forbidden). A later GO that counts the 6-cell battery, the PBO-alternative robustness story, or any A4-P2 survivor evidence is invalid as-is.

findings.title: Expense-cost convention asymmetry between the frozen cost ceilings and the committed stress net
findings.description: The P2 cost ceilings (binding for the A4-P2 R1/R5 family-kill route) INCLUDE expense_bps_over_holding in round_trip_cost_ceiling_bps. The committed cost_path_control computes an explicit expense line but excludes it from net_stress_usd_total (= gross - execution - path). arms.py declares path/expense lines 'recorded_not_booked'. The anti-double-count rationale (ETP market prices already embed fees, so charging expense again would double count) is plausible but appears NOWHERE in the freeze or the cost contract; R5's text ('FULL measured path-cost ladder ... including every leg's Q-16 roll/decay path component') is silent on expense. The two A4 kill routes (ceiling clearance vs R5 stress net) therefore use inconsistent expense conventions and can disagree for a marginal arm. The convention must be pinned explicitly before any R5/family-kill verdict at E.
